title: paged-kv-cache-block-manager-reuse-pinning-refactor
author: Evelyn Chu
description: Motivation: the paged KV cache block manager has accumulated ad-hoc allocator logic which causes lock contention, increased fragmentation, and suboptimal pinning behavior under high-concurrency steady-state serving workloads. This PR refactors the block allocator to use per-shard arenas with size-class freelists, introduces a reuse-first allocation fast path, and centralizes pinning/TTL semantics to avoid unnecessary evictions during transient bursts. Summary of changes: 1) refactor allocator: split global allocator into N shard arenas (based on CPU/hardware topology), each with size-class freelists and a lightweight epoch-based reclamation to eliminate coarse-grained global locks; 2) reuse optimizations: implement a reuse fast-path that returns compatible blocks from freelists without touching the slow path and adds a best-fit heuristic for small/medium blocks to reduce fragmentation; 3) pinning and TTL: unify pinning metadata and add a pin-hint API so long-lived contexts can mark blocks to avoid eviction; add an adaptive TTL that extends recently-reused blocks to reduce churn; 4) eviction policy tweaks: change LRU sampling to prioritized sampling biased toward high-cost-to-reconstruct segments and add a safety floor for minimum pinned capacity to avoid head-of-line stalls; 5) observability and knobs: add per-shard allocator metrics (allocations, frees, contention-waits), pinning hit/miss rates, and config knobs for shard count/size-class thresholds/TTL multipliers; 6) tests and bench: microbenchmarks for continuous batching workloads and integration tests with the perf-canary harness. Results: in our internal perf-canary with 2k concurrent streaming requests and batch sizes matching production distributions, p95 token latency decreased by ~9% and throughput increased by ~15% compared to the previous allocator; memory fragmentation (measured as wasted bytes/active working set) reduced by ~22%; allocator lock contention metric fell by ~75% on 16-shard hosts. Backwards compatibility: API surface is unchanged; pin-hint is additive. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag and disabled by default on Dedicated for first 2 weeks; gradual rollout via canary pools and automatic rollback on error budget depletion. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups (heap-polishing, TTL tuning, cross-region behavior).

release_notes: Performance: Refactored paged KV block allocator to per-shard arenas and added reuse fast-path resulting in lower p95 latency and higher throughput. Reliability: unified pinning and adaptive TTL reduce cache churn for streaming workloads. Ops: added allocator metrics and runtime knobs. Rollout: feature gated, gradual canary rollout. API: no breaking changes; pin-hint API is additive.
